label: Higher after unrewarded trials at D1; higher at GO/D2 after choosing a1, lowest after rare-unrewarded a2.
terms: (phase == GO) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S1 r") ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 39 is dominated by timing (high at D1/GO, low at D2). Beyond timing: at D1 it rises when the previous trial was unrewarded (+0.11) and is lowest after a rare-rewarded a2 trial; at GO and D2 it is higher when the previous choice was a1 (+0.085) and sharply lower at GO after a2 -> S1 unrewarded (rare, unrewarded: model-based stay on a2), i.e. a graded a1-vs-a2 preference signal. The free fit adds the observer belief log-odds at GO/D2/D1 (positive = S1 good raises it), D1 after a2 S1 r, and the D2 choice a1; it reaches 0.65 dev vs 0.51 for the short form. Residual misses: under-predicted after a1 -> S2 trials (D1 and GO), over-predicted at D1 after a2 -> S1. No future variables used.

issues: The 'after choosing a1 at GO/D2' claim is a weaker stand-in for the observer's belief. Alone, (phase != D1)*(prev_action==1) scores 0.158 test, while (phase != D1)*belief_lo scores 0.312. Fitting both gives 0.317, so prev_action adds almost nothing once belief is in. The GO residual by belief decile runs smoothly from -0.10 to +0.10.

Putting belief_lo in place of the prev_action term in the recorded short form raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.512 to 0.542, so the recorded short form is not the best description of its own main effect.

Misses on the recorded short form show a large systematic error at D1 after a2->S1 trials: over-predicted by -0.101 (rewarded) and -0.079 (unrewarded). At D1 the lowest cell is a2 S1 r (-0.131), not rare-unrewarded a2. So 'lowest after rare-unrewarded a2' holds at GO only, and the label leaves the D1 a2->S1 dip out.

Also under-predicted: every cell after a1->S2 (D1 +0.06, GO +0.048, D2 +0.049). In the worst windows, a run of a2/S1-unrewarded trials gives GO values that keep falling (0.50 -> 0.33 -> 0.23 -> 0.20) while the prediction stays flat. That looks like accumulating evidence (belief), not a one-trial last_is effect.

Partly a fitted correction: the GO last_is('a2 S1 u') term and a D1 a2->S1 term each fix one cell, and either one leaves the other a2->S1 miss behind (with the D1 term in, GO after a2 S1 u is still -0.12).
Claims that hold: unrewarded raises it at D1 (+0.11 weight, alone 0.158 test), and the timing baseline gives R^2 0.92.
